resampling_unit: One joint disturbance scenario, shared by baseline and all interventions. Do not resample candidates as if independent observations.
top_five: Assign unit weight above the fifth-largest importance and share the remaining mass equally across all ties at that boundary. Overlap is the sum of the smaller weights divided by five. Also report boundary-tie counts.
pair_reversals: Compare every pair within each form. The denominator is the number of strictly ordered reference pairs. Report reversed pairs and tied proxy pairs separately. Equal values use tolerance 1e-12.
correlation: Spearman correlation with average ranks for ties. A constant variable gives an undefined correlation, reported as such.
event_error_aggregation: Report baseline and each form separately. Pooled counts cover all candidates and scenarios, and do not treat correlated candidate observations as independent for intervals.
formal_transfer_family: One primary adjacency model at service limit 1.10. Use one-sided Clopper-Pearson event-disagreement upper bounds with alpha=0.05/798 for the baseline and all 797 interventions. Shared scenarios do not invalidate the union bound.
approximations: First- and second-order scores retain the locked exact-DPC threshold and healthy normalisation. Report their importance error against exact DPC and against independently calculated service.
horizon_checks: Report all seven frozen factors under both fixed relative threshold and fixed raw threshold. No factor may be selected using these results.
direction_checks: Compare directed and reciprocal-rate-symmetrised service under the same directed disturbances and interventions. Report both service metrics independently of DPC.
allocation_checks: Compare proportional-headroom and uniform allocations with identical total increment, candidate and scenario. Keep all forms and all candidates.
